claims.statement: Adobe states that Service Account (JWT) credentials reached end of life on June 30, 2025 and are no longer supported; they cannot be created after June 3, 2024, and Adobe will convert remaining ones to OAuth Server-to-Server credentials after their certificates expire or on March 1, 2026, whichever is earlier.

sources.supports: As of June 30, 2025, Service Account (JWT) credentials have reached end of life; after June 3, 2024 no new ones can be created; automatic conversion after certificate expiry or March 1, 2026.
Notes that Service Account (JWT) credentials reached end of life and all server-to-server integrations must use OAuth Server-to-Server credentials.

claims.statement: The migration page contrasts the new credential with the Service Account (JWT) credential by saying the latter used a public certificate and private key pair to generate access tokens, that the developer downloaded and saved the private key, and that the pair had to be rotated every year.

sources.supports: The new credential does not use a public certificate and private key pair; you do not have to download and save the private key; the old credential needs the pair rotated every year.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Adobe documentation read for this candidate gives no prefix, alphabet, length or other format rule for this value; any example in it is a placeholder or a public identifier. Not researched beyond existence.

This is a deprecated credential type. Whether private keys from it still exist in the wild, what encoding they use, and whether any still authenticate after the stated conversion dates are not established by the pages read; a historical contract would need a durable pin of the then-current documentation. Not assumed current.
